tools.name: check_website
tools.description: Checks whether a public website responds right now, from the monitoring service, without an account. Returns status, HTTP code and timings. Free; limited to a few checks a minute.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Plan and its monitor slots (standard in plan_monitors, premium in premium_monitors with their kinds), and the workspace's time zone (workspace.time_zone), which report days follow. Call this first to know whether the plan has room for another monitor.

tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: Location codes you can pass in a monitor's `locations`.

tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: Every monitor with its current status (pending, up, down, degraded), and interval. Free.

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.description: One monitor with uptime for 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, its last 90 days, incident totals, its latest results with errors, recent incidents, and route traces from failing locations (Pro and Business: each hop's loss, round trips and jitter over every round). Free.

tools.name: get_monitor_results
tools.description: A monitor's most recent check results, newest first. Older results may be merged: repeats checks with the same outcome up to last_checked_at. Free.

tools.name: get_uptime_history
tools.description: A monitor's daily uptime, kept for as long as it exists: checks, successful, failed and average response time per UTC day, oldest first. By default from the first check to today. Free.

tools.name: get_sla_report
tools.description: Business plans: availability against an SLA target for a range of days in the workspace's time zone (time_zone in get_account; by default this month), with the downtime budget used and left, incidents, MTTR, MTBF and the longest outage, per monitor (lowest availability first) and overall. The dashbo

tools.name: get_error_budgets
tools.description: Every monitor with an availability objective (slo_target over slo_window_days, set with update_monitor): its availability over the rolling window, the error budget in seconds, how much is used and left, the last hour's burn rate and whether it burns fast, least budget left first. Every plan. Free.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: Outages, newest first, with their status (open, acknowledged, resolved). Free.

tools.name: acknowledge_incident
tools.description: Marks an open incident as being handled: its repeat alerts and escalation stop. Everyone alerted still hears when it recovers. Free.

tools.name: list_escalation_policies
tools.description: Business plans: escalation policies, whose id a monitor's escalation_policy_id takes, and their steps. Free.

tools.name: list_on_call_schedules
tools.description: Business plans: on-call schedules with who is on call now, until when, and who is next. Free.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident with its timeline (detected, acknowledged, comments, status page updates, recovered), root cause and post-mortem, and the status pages its updates go to with their subscriber counts. Free.

tools.name: post_incident_update
tools.description: Publishes an update on every published status page that shows the incident's monitor and in their RSS and Atom feeds, and on Pro plans emails those pages' subscribers. States: investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved. Write for the page's visitors. Free.

tools.name: comment_on_incident
tools.description: Adds a comment to the incident's timeline, seen only by the workspace (Pro plans). Use it to record what you found or did. Free.

tools.name: open_incident
tools.description: Opens an incident for what the checks cannot see: a slow service, a problem a customer reported. With a message it publishes the first update on the status pages that show its monitors (and emails their subscribers on Pro plans); alert pages the monitors' contacts once. It stays open until resolve_i

tools.name: update_incident
tools.description: Changes the title status pages show (public_title) or the root cause (Pro plans) of any incident, and the title, severity and monitors of one opened by hand. Fields left out keep their value. Free.

tools.name: resolve_incident
tools.description: Resolves an incident opened with open_incident; the contacts it alerted hear so. A message is published as the last update on its status pages. Incidents opened by checks resolve with their checks. Free.

tools.name: write_postmortem
tools.description: Writes a resolved incident's post-mortem: summary, impact, root cause and follow-ups (one per line), on Pro plans. It stays in the workspace until published: true shows it under the incident on the status pages that show it and in their feeds; false takes it off. Publish only when the user asks. Fre

tools.name: list_status_pages
tools.description: The workspace's status pages: their address (/status/{slug}), the monitors they show with the names visitors see, and their named groups of monitors in order. Free.

tools.name: update_status_page_components
tools.description: Replaces the monitors a status page shows, in order, each optionally in a named group ("API", "EU region"); a group sits where its first monitor is and shows their worst state. Every plan. Free.

tools.name: create_on_call_schedule
tools.description: Business plans: a rotation through notification contacts (list_notification_contacts), handing off daily or weekly at a time in a time zone. The first member is on call from now. Free.

tools.name: update_on_call_schedule
tools.description: Business plans. Fields left out keep their value; changing the members, rotation, handoff or time zone starts the rotation over. Free.

tools.name: delete_on_call_schedule
tools.description: Deletes a schedule no escalation policy uses. Free.

tools.name: add_on_call_override
tools.description: Business plans: puts a contact on call in a schedule from starts_at to ends_at (up to 90 days), instead of the rotation. Overrides may not overlap. Free.

tools.name: remove_on_call_override
tools.description: Removes an override from a schedule (its id is in the schedule's overrides). Free.

tools.name: create_escalation_policy
tools.description: Business plans: ordered steps, each alerting contacts and whoever is on call in schedules, then waiting for an acknowledgement before the next. Monitors use it with update_monitor's escalation_policy_id. Free.

tools.name: update_escalation_policy
tools.description: Business plans. Fields left out keep their value; steps replaces them all. Free.

tools.name: delete_escalation_policy
tools.description: Deletes a policy; its monitors go back to alerting their own contacts. Free.

tools.name: list_maintenance_windows
tools.description: Maintenance windows, latest first: times when failures open no incidents and send no alerts, for one monitor or all. A repeating window has its recurrence in words (repeats), its next occurrences and the ones skipped or moved. Free.

tools.name: create_maintenance_window
tools.description: Schedules maintenance for one monitor or all: no incidents or alerts while it lasts (suppress_alerts), and with announce the status pages that show it list it and tell their subscribers. With recurrence it repeats daily, weekly on chosen days or monthly, in the workspace's time zone (get_account), s

tools.name: update_maintenance_window
tools.description: Changes a maintenance window or every occurrence of a repeating one. Fields left out keep their value; recurrence null makes it a single window. Changing the times or recurrence undoes skipped and moved occurrences. Free.

tools.name: change_maintenance_occurrence
tools.description: Skips (skipped: true), moves (starts_at and ends_at) or changes the message of one occurrence of a repeating maintenance window, leaving the others as they are; restore: true undoes it. Free.

tools.name: delete_maintenance_window
tools.description: Deletes a maintenance window, every occurrence of a repeating one included. Subscribers told about an occurrence that has not started hear it is cancelled. Free.

tools.name: get_audit_log
tools.description: Who changed what in the workspace, newest first: people, API tokens and agents, with the changed fields and IP (Business plan). Filter by resource_type (monitor, alert_channel, status_page, member, api_token…), action (monitor.updated, or a prefix like monitor.), from and to (YYYY-MM-DD); pass next

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Creates a monitor in a free slot of the workspace's plan. Premium monitors (multi-step transactions and code repositories) have slots of their own, on Pro and Business only. When every slot is in use the call fails with monitor_limit_reached: the user can upgrade at https://upheron.com/pricing or de

tools.name: preview_monitor_import
tools.description: Reads the monitors of another service: UptimeRobot (a read-only API key, or its bulk upload CSV), Better Stack (a team-based API token), Uptime Kuma (its JSON backup) or a CSV file in UpHeron's format (https://upheron.com/docs/import). Creates nothing: says which would be created and which skipped a

tools.name: import_monitors
tools.description: Creates the monitors the user chose from preview_monitor_import (send their `monitor` objects). Each takes a plan slot like create_monitor; ones already monitored are skipped. Imported heartbeats get new URLs, returned once as heartbeat_url: tell the user to point their scheduled jobs at them. Needs

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.description: Changes a monitor's settings, within the plan's interval and location limits. Free.

tools.name: pause_monitor
tools.description: Stops checking a monitor. Free.

tools.name: resume_monitor
tools.description: Starts checking a paused monitor again. Free.

tools.name: delete_monitor
tools.description: Deletes a monitor and its history. Frees its plan slot.

tools.name: add_notification_contact
tools.description: Adds an email address, chat channel, paging service, Jira project, webhook or phone number to alert on outages and recoveries. Email contacts must open a confirmation link before they receive alerts. A phone number texts or calls through the user's own account with a provider, on every plan, which b

tools.name: confirm_notification_contact
tools.description: Confirms an sms or voice contact, added before they were retired, with the 6-digit code it was texted or told in a call. The code works for 24 hours and 5 tries. Ask the phone's owner for it; never guess.

tools.name: list_notification_contacts
tools.description: Contacts that receive alerts, whether each is confirmed, and for phone contacts their latest text or call and whether it was delivered.

tools.name: test_notification_contact
tools.description: Sends a contact a test alert, at most 5 a minute for a workspace. For a phone contact it is a real text or call through the user's account, which counts toward its 6 texts or 3 calls an hour; an error says in words what the provider refused (credentials, a trial account's unverified number, the send

tools.name: get_vulnerabilities
tools.description: For an http or api monitor with vulnerability_alerts on: the vulnerabilities and unsupported releases found in the website's software, actively exploited and most severe first, with the version that fixes each, and the software they were matched on (found by scanning the website, imported, or added)

tools.name: import_software
tools.description: Tells the monitor what software the website and its server run, so their vulnerabilities are checked. Send a file's contents (package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock, mix.lock, composer.json/.lock, requirements.txt, Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, Gemfile.lock, go.mod, Cargo.

tools.name: add_software
tools.description: Adds one piece of software the website runs, by name (Debian, nginx, WordPress, Next.js…), package (npm:lodash, composer:vendor/package, pypi:django, wp-plugin:slug) or NVD product (cpe:vendor:product), with its version if known. Replaces a detected or imported entry for the same product. Free.

tools.name: remove_software
tools.description: Removes an entry from get_vulnerabilities' software list. Software the scan found is ignored instead, so the next scan does not add it back. Free.

tools.name: mark_vulnerability_fixed
tools.description: Records that the software behind a finding from get_vulnerabilities was upgraded: to `version`, or by default to the first version that fixes it (the finding's fix_version). The monitor is checked again; findings that no longer apply disappear, and one that still applies stays, marked with the versi

tools.name: get_ports
tools.description: For a monitor with port_scan on (Business plans): which of its host's addresses are verified and how to verify the rest (a file each address serves, or reverse DNS under the host with a TXT record), the ports the last weekly scan found open, flagged where the service usually should not be public, an

tools.name: verify_host
tools.description: Looks for the proof of each of the host's addresses from get_ports: the file served at the address, or its reverse DNS (PTR) under the host resolving back to it with the TXT record in place. The TXT record alone proves no address. The proof must stay in place, since every scan checks it again; only

tools.name: get_website_changes
tools.description: For a website or API monitor: its security headers grade with what each missing or weak header does and how to fix it, its DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, NS, MX, SPF, DMARC) and the networks its addresses belong to, its page fingerprint (Business: title, external script hosts, and the latest change wa

tools.name: accept_page_change
tools.description: Makes the page as it is now the new baseline of a monitor with content_watch, after get_website_changes shows a change you or the site's owner made on purpose. Later looks compare with it. Free.

tools.name: scan_ports
tools.description: Scans the verified host's common TCP ports now instead of waiting for the weekly scan, at most once an hour. Takes a minute or two; then read get_ports. Free.

tools.name: get_domain_watch
tools.description: For an http or api monitor on Pro and Business plans: the website's registered domain, its subdomains from certificate transparency logs (crt.sh, which can be days or weeks behind) with where each points and any CNAME to a service that reports no site there (subdomain_alerts), and the registered typ

tools.name: scan_website_software
tools.description: Scans the monitor's website for the software it runs and checks it against the vulnerability sources now, instead of waiting for the next scan. Takes up to a minute; then read get_vulnerabilities. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_incident, open_incident, import_monitors, add_notification_contact, list_notification_contacts · Private data: comment_on_incident, open_incident, resolve_incident, create_on_call_schedule, add_on_call_override, create_escalation_policy, delete_escalation_policy, get_audit_log, create_monitor, preview_monitor_import, import_monitors, add_notification_contact, confirm_notification_contact, list_notification_contacts, test_notification_contact, import_software, mark_vulnerability_fixed, get_ports, verify_host, get_website_changes · Public sink: get_incident, post_incident_update, write_postmortem, list_maintenance_windows, preview_monitor_import, import_monitors, add_notification_contact, confirm_notification_contact, import_software · Destructive: delete_on_call_schedule, remove_on_call_override, delete_escalation_policy, delete_maintenance_window, create_monitor, preview_monitor_import, delete_monitor, import_software, remove_software.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_incident, open_incident, import_monitors, add_notification_contact, list_notification_contacts · Private data: comment_on_incident, open_incident, resolve_incident, create_on_call_schedule, add_on_call_override, create_escalation_policy, delete_escalation_policy, get_audit_log, create_monitor, preview_monitor_import, import_monitors, add_notification_contact, confirm_notification_contact, list_notification_contacts, test_notification_contact, import_software, mark_vulnerability_fixed, get_ports, verify_host, get_website_changes · Public sink: get_incident, post_incident_update, write_postmortem, list_maintenance_windows, preview_monitor_import, import_monitors, add_notification_contact, confirm_notification_contact, import_software · Destructive: delete_on_call_schedule, remove_on_call_override, delete_escalation_policy, delete_maintenance_window, create_monitor, preview_monitor_import, delete_monitor, import_software, remove_software

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
